For findWrapPos, I'm crafting specific text inputs to exercise each branch: early newlines within width, tabs without newlines at valid positions, short text below width, backward whitespace search, and forward whitespace fallback when no earlier break exists — all exercised through renderWrappedText and printWrapped.

For test D, I want a case where a space exists before the wrap boundary so the backward search finds it correctly, verifying word-boundary wrapping. For test E, I need a scenario where no whitespace exists before the boundary but one does appear afterward, so the function falls back to searching forward for the next break point.

Since the backward search fails and returns to startPos, the code falls back to a forward search instead, scanning ahead until it hits the first whitespace character, which in this example is the space after the long word at index 34 -- so it returns that position as the break point.

Now I'm testing the edge case where there's no whitespace at all in the entire text, meaning the forward search would run past the end of the string and potentially hit an out-of-bounds index when checking `charAt` at a position equal to the string's length.

So when pos equals text.length(), the loop condition pos<=text.length() still passes, but calling charAt at that index is invalid since valid indices only go up to length-1, throwing a StringIndexOutOfBoundsException. That points to an actual off-by-one bug in the original code.

This connects to the CLI-162 issue involving findWrapPos, where an exception is deliberately thrown when pos equals lastPos to prevent an infinite loop. That guard seems to be the fix targeting the Cli-23 bug, so I'm trying to figure out whether the underlying loop logic still has problems even with this exception in place.

A single word longer than the width without any spaces would cause the wrapping position calculation to stall at the same index repeatedly, which is exactly the documented scenario for triggering this RuntimeException. Rather than guessing at edge cases with borderline word lengths, I should construct a test using one long, unbroken word that exceeds the wrap width to explicitly trigger and assert on this documented exception behavior.

Tracing through a concrete example with an all-letter string and no whitespace confirms the backward search hits the start of the string without finding a break, decrementing pos below zero, which then forces the forward search to run off the end of the text and throw an out-of-bounds exception.

This confirms findWrapPos genuinely fails on a single unbroken word wider than the wrap width -- a real fault worth capturing as a test case for detecting this defect.

I'm uncertain about the exact exception type since this was derived through static analysis rather than actual execution, but I don't want to guess at the specific defect number without more certainty—better to write a test that simply checks whether it crashes rather than asserting on a specific exception type.

Since manual tracing suggests a StringIndexOutOfBoundsException would occur, I'll write the test with a comment noting this expected behavior, using an expected-exception annotation to document the deterministic failure.

I'm also double-checking the whitespace-scanning scenario to confirm the forward-search loop finds a space before running past the end of the text, verifying that case doesn't throw.

Now I'm designing a test targeting the explicit "pos == lastPos" infinite-loop guard, which throws a RuntimeException when the wrap position stops advancing across iterations. This happens when padding plus the remaining trimmed text repeatedly resolves to the same wrap position, so I'm constructing a text/width/tab-stop combination that reproduces that stuck state deliberately.

Maybe I should look at how the actual Commons CLI test suite reproduces CLI-162, using a small width with multi-line text containing blank lines, and try to mirror that exact scenario instead of guessing values myself.

I'll simplify by constructing a scenario where width is smaller than the tab stop, using a text with words all longer than the width so padding repeats, and trace through what happens manually with something like "aaaaaa bbbbbb cccccc" to see if it triggers the infinite loop.

Tracing through the wrap position calculation...

So pos lands at 6 since that's where the space after "aaaaaa" falls, and it's not equal to the text length, so it returns 6 as the first wrap point. The output builds by trimming and appending the first line, then padding the next line with 6 spaces to align with the tab stop before adding the remaining trimmed text.

Now working through the next wrap position: with the padded text of length 19, scanning backward from position 4 immediately hits a whitespace character (one of the leading padding spaces), so the loop stops right away and returns pos=4 since it's greater than the start position. This differs from the previous lastPos of 6, so it continues appending the trimmed substring up to that point.

But then reconstructing the text with padding plus the trimmed remainder produces the exact same 19-character string as before ("aaaaaa" width padding plus "bbbbbb cccccc"), and running findWrapPos again on this identical text yields the same pos=4. Since this new pos equals the previous lastPos of 4, this triggers the infinite loop guard and throws a RuntimeException -- confirming this specific combination of width=4, nextLineTabStop=6, and the text "aaaaaa bbbbbb cccccc" reproduces the bug. I'm planning to write a test case using either printWrapped or renderWrappedText directly to verify this exception is thrown.

Since the backward search hits index -1 without finding a space, it fails, so I move to the forward search: starting at index 4, I scan ahead through 'a','a' until hitting the space at index 6, confirming that pos=6 is returned, consistent with my earlier trace.

Now for the second iteration, I build the padding of 6 spaces and trim the remainder of the original text starting at index 6, giving "bbbbbb cccccc", then concatenate to form a new 19-character string with spaces at indices 0-5, b's at 6-11, a space at 12, and c's at 13-18.

Running findWrapPos again with startPos=4 and width=0: since startPos+width=4 is less than 19, I proceed to the backward search, but the character at index 4 is a space, so that loop condition fails immediately.

Since pos ends up equal to startPos(4) which is greater than 0, I return pos=4, and since this doesn't match lastPos(6) from before, no exception fires yet — I append the trimmed empty substring plus a newline, set lastPos=4, and reconstruct the text again with padding plus the trimmed remainder starting at index 4, continuing to trace through the indices to verify the b's and c's positions align as expected.

For the next round, text becomes padding(6)+substring(4).trim() of the current 19-char string, which works out to the same "      bbbbbb cccccc" string as before - so this iteration produces an identical result to the prior one.

That means findWrapPos will return pos=4 again, and since lastPos also equals 4, this triggers the exception on the third call rather than the second as I first assumed - but the final conclusion still holds: a RuntimeException gets thrown eventually, so the test with expected=RuntimeException.class should pass regardless of exact iteration count.

Rechecking the boundary condition "startPos + width >= text.length()": 5>=10 is false, so it proceeds as expected, confirming my earlier trace.
